papers.title: A penalty method for PDE-constrained optimization in inverse problems

verification.S2_record_title: A penalty method for PDE-constrained optimization in inverse problems
verification.version_or_year_conflict: S2 first year2015 matches preprint/online; Inverse Problems volume32 issue1 is2016. Failed Utrecht PDF403 retained; successful author arXiv PDF read.

papers.claim: Quadratic PDE penalties permit exact state elimination; their experiments include increasing-penalty continuation, and analysis concerns approximate stationarity of the constrained Lagrangian, not global optimization.

evidence.summary: Quadratic PDE penalties permit exact state elimination; their experiments include increasing-penalty continuation, and analysis concerns approximate stationarity of the constrained Lagrangian, not global optimization.

papers.study_context: General linear-state PDE inverse problems; acoustic seismic examples; direct augmented state solves and GN/QN; relaxed states may violate the PDE.

confidence.reason: Identifiable primary full-text method and limitation passages read

limitations: Penalty selection and robust continuation remain issues; additional outer stages have cost.
Convexity in the state block does not imply joint/material convexity.
R2 already implemented exact full-current elimination at fixed CIE weight; ordinary-LSIE penalty continuation is an established different control, not a new invention.
papers.analyst_inference: A predeclared ordinary-LSIE current-penalty continuation with original-physics final correction is a reasonable small control against equal extra ordinary work; no recovery prediction follows.

papers.title: An analysis of constraint-relaxation in PDE-based inverse problems

verification.S2_record_title: An analysis of constraint-relaxation in PDE-based inverse problems
verification.version_or_year_conflict: Read arXiv v1 titled A data-driven approach to PDE-constrained optimization in inverse problems, first posted2024; canonical journal title/year2025 verified independently. Do not present v1 passages as final journal text.

papers.evidence_location: primary_texts/metric2024.html §2.4 Cor1 Eq10; §2.6 Thm3; §2.7 Cor2 Eq13 Remarks2–4; §3.3.2 Eq21; extracted section2_7/section3_3 text and METRIC_CONVEXITY_HANDOFF.md
papers.claim: Eliminating relaxed states yields a parameter-dependent inverse-Gram residual metric. A special finite solution space equal to the span of source/measurement Riesz functions makes the zero-penalty objective quadratic in an affine PDE coefficient when the inner product is coefficient-independent.

evidence.summary: Eliminating relaxed states yields a parameter-dependent inverse-Gram residual metric. A special finite solution space equal to the span of source/measurement Riesz functions makes the zero-penalty objective quadratic in an affine PDE coefficient when the inner product is coefficient-independent.

papers.study_context: Weak PDE formulation; same indexed source/measurement functionals; well-posedness, finite measurements, noiseless interpretation. Case studies include elliptic,1D Helmholtz and Schrodinger problems.

confidence.reason: Identifiable primary full-text method and limitation passages read

limitations: Remark2 explicitly gives no guarantee of identifiability or adequate physical approximation for that finite solution space.
General PDE-residual projection space W_n depends on the current coefficient.
Helmholtz data-Gram Eq21 needs frequency derivatives plus boundary responses/derivatives and boundary speed.
v1 Eq23–24 omit the inverse appearing in general Eq10; retained as a source inconsistency, not silently repaired.
Project exterior rectangular port response does not automatically furnish this square matched-functional Galerkin contract.
papers.analyst_inference: The data-driven fixed Gram and finite source/measurement-span Galerkin linear fit are structurally more specific than a scalar penalty schedule, but acquisition/approximation qualification is required before implementation.

papers.title: Cross-Correlated Contrast Source Inversion

verification.version_or_year_conflict: Journal2017; author arXiv upload2019 refers to the same paper.

papers.claim: CC-CSI adds a measurement-domain mismatch built from the constitutive one-step current prediction to ordinary data and state errors; PR current updates and modified material gradients are given.

evidence.summary: CC-CSI adds a measurement-domain mismatch built from the constitutive one-step current prediction to ordinary data and state errors; PR current updates and modified material gradients are given.

papers.study_context: 2D scalar TM and TE numerical microwave inverse scattering; comparison with CSI and MR-CSI, not this project A/A+.

confidence.reason: Identifiable primary full-text method and limitation passages read

limitations: A small state residual can have large measurement-domain effect; the extra mismatch targets this problem.
The paper does not prove arbitrary Maxwell global convexity.
The extra mismatch uses background propagation of constitutive current, not the full physical resolvent at the candidate material.
Already covered as prior art in R2/R3; do not call adding current/data coupling new.
papers.analyst_inference: Useful mature control if a state/data consistency mechanism is claimed; final original-Maxwell data/material metrics remain necessary.

papers.title: The Cross-Entropy Method for Combinatorial and Continuous Optimization

verification.S2_record_title: The Cross-Entropy Method for Combinatorial and Continuous Optimization

papers.evidence_location: Springer publisher abstract; full algorithm/proof NOT read
papers.claim: The cross-entropy optimization method uses KL-based auxiliary optimization, importance sampling and distribution/temperature adjustment to search nonconvex problems on bounded domains.

evidence.summary: The cross-entropy optimization method uses KL-based auxiliary optimization, importance sampling and distribution/temperature adjustment to search nonconvex problems on bounded domains.

papers.study_context: Generic continuous and combinatorial global optimization, not a Maxwell material-recovery benchmark.

confidence.reason: Publisher abstract only; formulas and proof conditions not inspected

limitations: A convex bounded domain is not a convex objective.
Abstract global-convergence claim is tied to its combinatorial Markov-chain construction, not an arbitrary finite-sample continuous implementation.
No retrieved primary evidence establishes practical576-pixel full-wave global recovery or population cost under this project budget.
papers.analyst_inference: If tested, use a prespecified distribution family and count every failed and accepted full-wave sample; compare with equal-cost random/multistart proposals. It changes search, not the original objective into a convex function.

papers.title: Sinkhorn Distances: Lightspeed Computation of Optimal Transport

verification.S2_record_title: Sinkhorn Distances: Lightspeed Computation of Optimal Transport

papers.claim: Entropic regularization makes the transport-plan optimization strictly convex and permits efficient Sinkhorn matrix scaling for histogram comparison.

evidence.summary: Entropic regularization makes the transport-plan optimization strictly convex and permits efficient Sinkhorn matrix scaling for histogram comparison.

papers.study_context: Probability histograms, transport plans and MNIST classification; not wave inversion.

confidence.reason: Identifiable primary full-text method and limitation passages read

limitations: The convex variable is the transport matrix with fixed marginals.
This does not prove convexity of a loss composed with a nonlinear Maxwell map in material variables.
Raw signed/complex fields are not probability histograms.
papers.analyst_inference: Only use as a clearly changed data discrepancy after specifying a positive, phase/amplitude-aware encoding and retained physical loss; entropy temperature belongs to the inner transport problem, not a material convexity certificate.

papers.title: Analysis of seismic inversion with optimal transportation and softplus encoding

verification.S2_record_title: Analysis of seismic inversion with optimal transportation and softplus encoding
verification.version_or_year_conflict: S2 first year2020 is arXiv; final Inverse Problems37 095004 published2021; journal DOI and title verified.

papers.claim: Softplus and normalization encode real seismograms as probability measures for Wasserstein loss; convexity discussion concerns translations/dilations and its asymptotic encoding behavior, with numerical Marmousi inversion.

evidence.summary: Softplus and normalization encode real seismograms as probability measures for Wasserstein loss; convexity discussion concerns translations/dilations and its asymptotic encoding behavior, with numerical Marmousi inversion.

papers.study_context: Acoustic time-domain real traces and kinematic cycle skipping, not complex single-frequency Maxwell.

confidence.reason: Identifiable primary full-text method and limitation passages read

limitations: Encoding and normalization can change which amplitude information contributes to the misfit.
Finite-window endpoints and encoding can spoil translation/dilation convexity; large softplus slope risks vanishing gradients/overflow.
Improved shift landscape is not global convexity in an arbitrary spatial material.
papers.analyst_inference: Geometry-aware discrepancy is a separate candidate mechanism from CE population search. Applying it to receiver/source complex ports needs an explicit observable-preserving encoding; do not silently discard phase.

papers.evidence_location: primary_texts/relative_entropy2021.txt §2 Eq1–7; §3 numerical setup and tuning; §4 conclusions lines1641–1645
papers.claim: Relative-entropy expressions are used as deterministic penalties incorporating reference/well information alongside ordinary L2 waveform misfit. The authors report a failed first quadratic entropy variant and path dependence, alongside better variants in synthetic BP-model studies.

evidence.summary: Relative-entropy expressions are used as deterministic penalties incorporating reference/well information alongside ordinary L2 waveform misfit. The authors report a failed first quadratic entropy variant and path dependence, alongside better variants in synthetic BP-model studies.

papers.study_context: Acoustic synthetic BP2004 subregions, known reference/well information and tuned dynamic regularization weights.

confidence.reason: Identifiable primary full-text method and limitation passages read

limitations: Extra material reference information is not free and differs from data-only physical inversion.
Raw unnormalized entropy expressions are not automatically nonnegative KL divergences.
One quadratic variant has two minimum regions and fails one test; the paper itself does not support entropy always removes local minima.
This is neither CE population search nor CE loss on complex field probabilities.
papers.analyst_inference: A legitimate public material prior could be added as a separately identified prior experiment; using hidden test support/GT as the reference would invalidate the comparison.
